daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has proposed two new vice presidential candidates to replace Gibran, nominating Agriculture Minister Amran Sulaiman and Defence Minister Sugiono to the MPR. The MPR has ruled that neither minister needs to resign from their current cabinet positions to run for vice president. Both candidates will be asked to sign commitment statements to prevent them from withdrawing from the race.

  • DPR Deputy Speaker Dasco confirmed that President Prabowo had discussed several alternative vice presidential names before settling on the two nominees, and Dasco himself stated he has no interest in becoming a vice presidential candidate.
  • Indonesia has named six senior police officers as treason suspects, including former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit, with investigators alleging they prepared 500 ACAB t-shirts to infiltrate demonstrations and had held meetings analyzing the 1998 crisis and impeachment scenarios before Prabowo's inauguration.
  • Police will convene an ethics hearing today for Brigadier General Tedjo Kusumo in the treason case, while Commissioner General Hendro Pandowo will chair the ethics trial for General Listyo Sigit on Thursday.
  • DPR Deputy Speaker Dasco has requested Commission III review the Police Law following a Constitutional Court ruling that declared the legislation formally flawed.
  • Agriculture Minister Amran pledged to continue serving farmers despite his vice presidential nomination.
  • A proposal for three vice presidents has sparked controversy for being unconstitutional and potentially causing conflict.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia is targeting at least US$3.8 billion in annual export gains from the Indonesia-EU Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (IEU-CEPA), with the government confirming that Indonesia is ready to meet sanitary and phytosanitary standards required under the agreement. Indonesia and the EU are poised to enter a new phase of strategic partnership as the trade agreement takes effect.

  • The Indonesian military (TNI) is seeking stronger defence cooperation through military diplomacy initiatives.
  • Indonesia is pursuing technology gains through digital diplomacy efforts.
  • Indonesia signed its participation contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, building on $28 billion in investment commitments secured at Expo 2025 Osaka.
  • TNI Commander explained the considerations behind changing terminology from OPM to Armed Extremist Group for separatists in Papua.

Other

The government is easing year-end travel with a transport fare stimulus, as announced by the minister to facilitate seasonal mobility. Meanwhile, the DPR has urged the government to accelerate spending in order to sustain economic growth amid concerns about budget execution rates.

  • Indonesia's tourism campaign in China has secured 13,650 trip bookings from the promotional effort.
  • Indonesia Deposit Insurance Corporation (LPS) has cancelled plans to build an office in IKN and will redirect the investment to Jakarta after the new capital was removed from government priorities.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs has found special hajj pilgrims who have not met the minimum age requirement of 16 years, prompting the ministry to update the list of pilgrims entitled to depart in 2027.
  • The National Narcotics Agency (BNN) has seized 11 vehicles and a coffee shop from an international drug trafficker in a major money laundering case.
  • Indonesia aims to strengthen horticulture product quality through the Horticultural Data Development Acceleration Program (HDDAP).
